newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA hits new low after currency comments.
newsitem.headline: SIA hits new low after currency comments.

text.p: Foreign shares in national carrier Singapore Airlines Ltd SIA) fell to their lowest point for almost a year on Thursday morning on a bout of selling by overseas funds, dealers said.
By 0125 GMT, the company's foreign share tranche, most widely followed by fund managers, was down 20 cents at Singapore $12.40. The local tranche was down 10 cents at S$7.35.
SIA's foreign shares have now dropped S$1.60 in four days following the announcement of poor half-year results on Monday.
The latest fall comes after the publication of gloomy comments by SIA's chief executive in a Reuters interview.
Cheong Choong Kong told Reuters on Wednesday the strength of the Singapore dollar and the weakness of the Japanese yen and the German mark were all hitting the company's performance.
High jet fuel prices and a weak cargo market were also both negative factors, Cheong said.

Dealers said the latest bout of selling, which produced a turnover of 1.3 million shares in the first half hour of trading on Thursday, had mainly come from overnight sell orders from foreign investors.
